admission_summary.conclusion: The base DNS RFCs use dynamic TTL/SOA/header values for most timed duties. Fixed retransmission and failure-cache rules either have no matching dnsmasq path or were standardized after the locked 2015 snapshot. No candidate simultaneously has a standard constant, a matching source timer, and a finite non-punctual pointwise formula.

implementation.selection: Exact ProFuzzBench DNS target snapshot, accessed through the imp/dnsmasq GitHub mirror.
implementation.repository_status: imp/dnsmasq is a GitHub mirror of the upstream official dnsmasq Git repository. The pinned SHA is an official dnsmasq-history snapshot mirrored to GitHub; imp/dnsmasq is not presented as an official GitHub origin.

record.method: Exhaustive numeric-timing screening of resolver retry/backoff, positive and negative TTL expiry, SOA refresh/retry/expire, failure and dead-server caching, DNS-over-TCP idle/keepalive, validation-derived expiry, and later serve-stale/failure-cache RFCs. Count-only limits and DHCP/TFTP timers in the combined dnsmasq codebase were outside DNS scope.

screening_records.numeric_rule: Without better history, the minimum UDP retransmission interval should be 2-5 seconds.
source_evidence: src/config.h:24 defines TIMEOUT=10 for forwarding-record retirement, not retransmission.
src/forward.c:304-315 reacts to a repeated downstream query and has no autonomous 2-5-second retry task.

screening_records.numeric_rule: If RTT information is unavailable, retry default should be no less than 5 seconds and use bounded exponential backoff.
source_evidence: The locked forwarder does not schedule its own upstream UDP retransmission; client retransmission triggers the retry path.

screening_records.numeric_rule: RFC 1035 suggested an idle period on the order of two minutes; RFC 7766 replaces it with seconds and deliberately gives no particular value.
source_evidence: src/config.h:19 and src/dnsmasq.c:1687-1723 impose a 150-second total child lifetime, not a reset-on-complete-message idle timer.

screening_records.numeric_rule: Cached RRs expire after their message-carried TTL in seconds; TTL is administrator/data selected rather than a standard constant.
source_evidence: src/cache.c:452-468 and 603-607 compute ttd=now+ttl from the dynamic input.
src/cache.c:314-323 and 633-660 reject entries after that dynamic deadline.

screening_records.numeric_rule: An RR with TTL zero is usable only for the current transaction and MUST NOT be cached.
source_evidence: Any positive-width interval would invent an epsilon absent from the standard; a zero-width singleton is forbidden by the extraction schema.

screening_records.numeric_rule: Secondary refresh, retry, and expiry delays are the SOA REFRESH, RETRY, and EXPIRE fields.
source_evidence: The RFC gives dynamic zone fields, and the locked dnsmasq source has no secondary-zone transfer state machine to map them to.

screening_records.numeric_rule: Negative-cache lifetime is min(SOA TTL, SOA.MINIMUM) and is decremented to zero.
source_evidence: src/rfc1035.c:866-917 extracts the dynamic minimum and src/rfc1035.c:1152-1168 passes it to cache_insert.

screening_records.numeric_rule: One to three hours is described as a sensible tunable default, not a universal mandatory value.
source_evidence: src/option.c:4376-4398 zero-initializes neg_ttl; without an SOA, the locked default therefore does not select a 1-3-hour profile.

screening_records.numeric_rule: If a resolver optionally caches a server failure, it MUST NOT do so longer than five minutes.
source_evidence: No fixed SERVFAIL-cache object or five-minute expiry path exists in the locked source.

screening_records.numeric_rule: A server may be considered unreachable after 120 seconds and, if cached, MUST NOT remain so longer than five minutes.
source_evidence: The locked forwarder has no matching per-server 120-second detection plus five-minute dead-server cache state.

screening_records.numeric_rule: Validation-derived cache TTL is a minimum of received TTLs and signature expiration; validation-failure cache TTL is only required to be small.
source_evidence: All endpoints are message-carried or unspecified; no fixed integer interval can be instantiated without inventing a profile.

screening_records.numeric_rule: The EDNS0 keepalive timeout is server selected in 100-millisecond units, not a fixed default.
source_evidence: The locked 2015 snapshot predates RFC 7828 and has no edns-tcp-keepalive option path.

screening_records.numeric_rule: The RFC recommends 30-second stale TTL and failure recheck, a 1.8-second client timer, a 7-day TTL clamp, and a 1-3-day stale window.
source_evidence: The locked 2015 snapshot predates RFC 8767 and contains no serve-stale state machine.

screening_records.numeric_rule: Resolution failures MUST be cached for at least one second and no longer than five minutes.
source_evidence: The locked 2015 snapshot predates RFC 9520 by more than eight years and has no matching failure-cache path.

screening_records.numeric_rule: The BCP limits unnecessary requery behavior but supplies no fixed elapsed-time interval; zero-TTL handling reduces to the punctual case above.
source_evidence: No additional non-punctual numeric duty remains after the RFC 1035/1123 retry and TTL candidates.
